1.0.0.en: The elder: an older person or a priest, because the Greek original carries both meanings, and what is meant is St. John, who held the headship of the priesthood and at the same time was advanced in age. Kyria: in the Greek original it means a lady.

1.0.1.en: This is the only book in the Bible sent to a lady. She is either a particular lady or it means the Church everywhere, and her children signify the believers in the whole world, who are chosen by God for eternal life. St. John writes to them declaring his love for them, and indeed the love of the believers in the Church of Ephesus and everywhere, who have believed in Christ, who is the truth, and loved Him.

1.1.0.en: The purpose of the epistle appears: to establish the believers in the truth, who is Christ, that they may live with Him and in Him forever.

1.2.0.en: In order to abide in Christ we need His grace and mercy, and the result of our life in Him is that we are at peace. All these blessings we receive from God the Father and His Son Jesus Christ, our Savior on the Cross, through His love poured out for us and His satisfying of divine justice, so that we live in the truth in Him.

1.2.1.en: Take care to know God through prayer and the Bible, and grow in both, so that your love for Him increases, you feel His presence in your life, and your heart is filled with peace.

1.2.2.en: (2) Truth and love (vv. 4-6:) 4 I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in truth, as we have received a commandment from the Father. 5 And now I beseech thee, lady, not as though I wrote a new commandment unto thee, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another. 6 And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.

1.3.0.en: The Apostle encourages this lady, or the Church, by his joy at the walk of her children in the truth, that is, the Christian walk. We note that he begins with encouragement before warning against the deceivers.

1.4.0.en: He reminds her and her children of the most important commandment of Christ, which they learned from the time they began the faith, and it is love for others.

1.5.0.en: Love for God, or love for others, has its details stated in the commandments, that is, the Bible, and Christ and His Apostles have commanded us to walk in it since we believed.

1.5.1.en: Love is the goal of all dealings with others. So before you speak with anyone, remember your goal, which is love, and give up every discussion that hinders it, forgive others their mistakes, and take care to encourage them with your kind words.

1.6.0.en: In the preceding verses the Apostle stressed the importance of holding fast to the truth, because of the appearance in the Church of heretics who deny the divinity of Christ and His Incarnation. These are the antichrists who try to lead the believers astray.

1.7.0.en: He warns the believers not to listen to the heretics, lest their faith and their eternity be lost, but rather to resist these misleading ideas with all strength and to warn those among them who were influenced, so that they return to the right faith. By this they receive a great reward in heaven for their spiritual vigilance and for bringing back to the Church the souls that had gone astray.

1.8.0.en: He also warns them to hold fast to the teachings of the Church, so that they enjoy God's blessings in their lives, whether through the sacraments of the Church or the constant work of the Holy Spirit in them. But whoever accepts the error of heresies and denies the divinity of Christ is deprived of all God's blessings in the New Covenant, which we receive through the blood of Christ the Redeemer.

1.9.0.en: He emphasizes his commands to shun the heretics, whether by not bringing them into our houses or by not greeting them, meaning not associating with them with much warmth, for this makes them feel that they are accepted by the Church, and this misleads the simple in the faith, so that they think their teachings are sound. The shunning here carries no malice in the heart, but firmness with love, and we pray for them that they may repent, while declaring our complete rejection of their false teachings. Any laxity in associating with them and accepting them makes us share in their errors, in the sense of causing the simple to stumble and be led astray.

1.9.1.en: Be loving toward everyone, humble and forbearing toward all, but be definite in your rejection of heresies and teachings foreign to the Church, and in avoiding meetings and teachings that do not agree with her, even if they are led by servants gifted in preaching who show love and concern for you. There must be no laxity in the faith that we received from our fathers the Apostles, and for which many were martyred.

1.10.0.en: In his preceding words the Apostle focused on the importance of holding fast to the truth, on words of love, and on rejecting the teachings of the deceivers. But he has many teachings that he gave them orally when he met them, and this is what is called Church tradition, that is, the teachings of the Apostles that were not written in the Bible and were handed down by the Fathers from generation to generation until now, because it is not possible to confine all the teachings of the Church to one book, the Bible. The Apostles referred to Church tradition, as in (Titus 1:5).

1.11.0.en: By "thy elect sister" is meant the Church in Ephesus, from which the Apostle wrote this epistle, and her children are the believers, members of the Church. He called her the elect because she is the Church of God, which He chose to be a bride for Him and to enjoy eternity with Him. Here appears the importance of relationships of love between the churches throughout the world that have one faith.

1.11.1.en: This is if what is meant by "Kyria" at the beginning of the epistle is the Church in the whole world. But if what is meant is a particular believing lady and her believing children, then the explanation of (v. 13) is her believing relatives living in Ephesus. In any case, what is meant in this verse is the greeting of the believers in Ephesus to the believers in general everywhere, who are signified by a particular lady or a particular church.

1.11.2.en: Take care to learn from the fathers and spiritual brethren on every occasion, for you receive from them the manner of Christian love and upright conduct in the various circumstances of life.
